title: Tool Calling
description: Learn how to build a tool-calling loop that enables Claude to interact with your local environment by executing scripts and processing their output.
learning_objectives: Define tools using JSON schema for LLM consumption
Implement the request-response cycle of a function-calling loop
Execute local shell commands safely via an AI agent
Feed tool outputs back into the model context to generate final answers
prerequisites: Basic proficiency in Python or Node.js
Experience making API calls to Claude/Anthropic

sections.heading: What is Tool Calling?
sections.content_brief: Explain the conceptual difference between an LLM generating code and 'Tool Calling' where the model requests a specific action. Clarify that the LLM does not execute the code itself, but provides the arguments for the client to do so.

sections.heading: Defining Tool Schemas
sections.content_brief: Demonstrate how to describe a tool's purpose and parameters using JSON schema. Explain why clear descriptions are critical for the model to select the correct tool and provide valid arguments.
sections.code_context: A definition of a 'run_script' tool including name, description, and input parameters.

sections.heading: Implementing the Tool Loop
sections.content_brief: Walk through the iterative process: sending the prompt with tools, detecting a 'tool_use' response, executing the local function, and sending the result back to the model. Detail the state management required to keep track of the conversation history.
sections.code_context: A complete loop that handles the transition from user input to tool execution and final response.

sections.heading: Building a Local Script Executor
sections.content_brief: Create a practical implementation of a tool that executes local shell commands or Python scripts. Show how to capture stdout and stderr to provide the model with full visibility into the result.
sections.code_context: A function using the subprocess module to run a command and return its output as a string.

sections.heading: Error Handling and Self-Correction
sections.content_brief: Discuss how to handle tool failures by passing error messages back to the model. Explain how this allows Claude to 'self-correct' by adjusting arguments or trying a different approach based on the error output.
sections.code_context: An example of passing a Python Traceback back to the model to trigger a fix.

admonitions.content: Never allow an LLM to execute arbitrary shell commands on a production system without strict sandboxing or human-in-the-loop approval, as this creates a critical security vulnerability.
When writing tool descriptions, use imperative language (e.g., 'Use this tool to fetch...') and be explicit about the expected format of the input parameters.
